clue_checks.clue: I lived before a great flood.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 7:6 says Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came, so he lived before it. Enoch also fits this clue alone, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: God told me to build with gopher wood.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 6:14: 'Make thee an ark of gopher wood.' In context (6:13), God is speaking to Noah.

clue_checks.clue: My sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 6:10 names Noah's three sons exactly.

clue_checks.clue: I built the ark.
clue_checks.reason: Hebrews 11:7 says Noah 'prepared an ark,' which matches the paraphrase 'built the ark.'

clue_checks.clue: An angel found me threshing wheat by a winepress.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 6:11-12 says Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress when the angel of the LORD appeared to him.

clue_checks.clue: I tested God with a fleece.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 6:36-40 describes Gideon proving God with a fleece twice, and 'let me prove' matches 'tested'.

clue_checks.clue: My army was reduced to three hundred men.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 7:7 has the LORD saving Israel by the three hundred and sending the rest home, which implies the reduction.

clue_checks.clue: We carried trumpets, pitchers and lamps.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 7:16 says each of the three hundred had a trumpet and an empty pitcher with a lamp inside.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Nazarite from birth.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:17: 'I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb.'

clue_checks.clue: I tore a young lion with my bare hands.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 14:5-6: he 'rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand.'

clue_checks.clue: Delilah learned the secret of my strength.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:17-18: he told her all his heart, and Delilah saw that he had done so.

clue_checks.clue: I pulled down the house where the Philistines gathered.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:29-30: he bowed himself on the pillars, and the house fell upon the lords and all the people therein.

clue_checks.clue: I was a woman of Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:4 names Ruth as one of the wives taken 'of the women of Moab.' Orpah also fits, but this is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I told my mother-in-law: whither thou goest, I will go.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:16 quotes Ruth saying 'whither thou goest, I will go' to Naomi, her mother-in-law.

clue_checks.clue: I gleaned in the fields of Boaz.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:3 says she gleaned and happened on 'a part of the field belonging unto Boaz.' The plural 'fields' is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I became an ancestor of King David.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13-17 says Ruth bore Obed, 'the father of Jesse, the father of David,' making her David's great-grandmother.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophetess.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:4 calls Deborah 'a prophetess.' Miriam and Huldah were also prophetesses, but this is the first clue, so that overlap is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I judged Israel under a palm tree in mount Ephraim.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:5 says she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah in mount Ephraim and Israel came up to her for judgment. Together with 4:4 ('she judged Israel'), this is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I summoned Barak to fight Sisera.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:6-7 says she sent and called Barak and conveyed the LORD's command to go against Sisera.

clue_checks.clue: A song of mine is recorded in Judges 5.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 5:1 says 'Then sang Deborah and Barak.' The song is shared with Barak, but calling it 'a song of mine' is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen when I was called.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:19 says Elisha was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen when Elijah cast his mantle upon him, which was his call.

clue_checks.clue: I asked for a double portion of my master's spirit.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:9 records Elisha asking Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.

clue_checks.clue: I took up the mantle that fell from Elijah.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:13 says he took up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him. In context (v.12) the 'he' is Elisha.

clue_checks.clue: I told Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:10 says Elisha sent a messenger telling Naaman to wash in Jordan seven times. Saying 'I told' when he spoke through a messenger is acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: As a baby I was hidden in an ark of bulrushes.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:3 says his mother, unable to hide him longer, put the child in an ark of bulrushes. Exodus 2:2 records the earlier hiding, and the identity of the child as Moses is clear from Exodus 2:10.

clue_checks.clue: I was raised in Pharaoh's household.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:10 says he was brought to Pharaoh's daughter and 'became her son,' and names him Moses. That reasonably supports being raised in Pharaoh's household (cf. Acts 7:21-22).

clue_checks.clue: I saw a bush burn without being consumed.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:2 states the bush burned with fire and was not consumed, and Exodus 3:3-4 names Moses as the one who saw it.

clue_checks.clue: I led Israel out of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 7:36 says 'He brought them out' of Egypt. The shown verse uses only a pronoun, and Moses is named in Acts 7:35 ('This Moses'). The clue is accurate in context, but the displayed text alone does not name him.

clue_checks.clue: My mother Hannah prayed for me at Shiloh.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:9-11 places Hannah in Shiloh, praying and vowing for a man child. 1:20 says she bore Samuel 'because I have asked him of the LORD.'

clue_checks.clue: As a boy I served Eli the priest.
clue_checks.reason: The KJV says the child 'did minister unto the LORD before Eli the priest.' He served the LORD under Eli's oversight, not Eli directly. This is an acceptable paraphrase but slightly loose.

clue_checks.clue: I heard the LORD call my name in the night.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 3:10 records the LORD calling 'Samuel, Samuel.' The night setting comes from the context (3:3, Samuel lying down to sleep), not from the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: I anointed both Saul and David.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 explicitly names David. 1 Samuel 10:1 says Samuel anointed 'him' without naming Saul in the verse shown; the context (chapter 9) identifies him as Saul. The clue is accurate, but the displayed text does not name Saul.

clue_checks.clue: I left Ur of the Chaldees.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 11:31 says Abram went forth from Ur of the Chaldees. Lot also went, but an early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: God changed my name.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 17:5 records God changing Abram's name to Abraham. Jacob's renaming (Gen 32:28) makes this ambiguous alone, but later clues resolve it.

clue_checks.clue: My wife laughed at God's promise of a son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 18:12 says Sarah laughed, and 'my lord being old' identifies Abraham. The promise itself is in v.10, but the laughter is clearly a response to it, so this is minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: God tested me in the land of Moriah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 22:1-2 says God did tempt (test) Abraham and sent him to the land of Moriah.

clue_checks.clue: I was born holding my twin brother's heel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:26 says his hand took hold on Esau's heel at birth and he was named Jacob. The surrounding context (25:24) establishes that they were twins.

clue_checks.clue: I bought my brother's birthright with pottage.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 says Esau sold his birthright unto Jacob, and Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles.

clue_checks.clue: I dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 28:12 describes the dream of a ladder whose top reached to heaven. The context (28:10) identifies the dreamer as Jacob.

clue_checks.clue: God renamed me Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:10 says God told Jacob his name would no more be called Jacob, but Israel.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 13:8 names Oshea the son of Nun among the twelve spies, and 13:16 says Moses renamed him Jehoshua (Joshua). It also fits Caleb, but only as an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I succeeded Moses as leader.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 1:1-2 shows that after Moses' death the LORD commanded Joshua to lead all the people over Jordan, which establishes him as Moses' successor.

clue_checks.clue: The walls of Jericho fell when the people shouted.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 6:16 has Joshua commanding the people to shout, and 6:20 records that the wall fell down flat at the shout. This ties the event to Joshua.

clue_checks.clue: I said: As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
clue_checks.reason: The clue quotes Joshua 24:15 directly.

clue_checks.clue: I was my father's favourite son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:3 says Israel loved Joseph more than all his children. Jacob's later special love for Benjamin (Gen 44:20) does not undermine this, and only this early clue could fit Benjamin.

clue_checks.clue: My brothers sold me into slavery.
clue_checks.reason: The passage shows Judah proposing the sale and the brothers agreeing. However, v.28's 'they drew... and sold' is grammatically ambiguous (it could refer to the Midianites), and 'slavery' is not explicit in the shown text. Genesis 45:4 ('whom ye sold into Egypt') would make the brothers' role explicit. The clue is still substantially supported.

clue_checks.clue: I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 41:25 shows Joseph beginning his interpretation of Pharaoh's dream.

clue_checks.clue: I was set over all the land of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 41:41 matches the clue verbatim in substance.

clue_checks.clue: I was a cunning hunter.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:27 says 'Esau was a cunning hunter.' Nimrod was also a hunter ('a mighty hunter,' Gen 10:9), but a single early clue fitting another option is acceptable, and the exact wording matches Esau.

clue_checks.clue: I was born red and hairy.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:25 says the first twin 'came out red, all over like an hairy garment' and was named Esau.

clue_checks.clue: I sold my birthright for a meal.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 says Esau 'sold his birthright unto Jacob' and then received bread and pottage of lentiles. 'A meal' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I am also called Edom.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 36:1 says 'Esau, who is Edom.'

clue_checks.clue: My house was upon the town wall of Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:15 says her house was upon the town wall. The surrounding passage (2:1-3) establishes that the city is Jericho.

clue_checks.clue: I hid two Israelite spies.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:4 says she took the two men and hid them. Verses 1-2 identify them as spies sent by Joshua, of the children of Israel.

clue_checks.clue: I let them down by a cord through a window.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:15 says this almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: A line of scarlet thread marked my home.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:18 has her bind the line of scarlet thread in the window, and 2:21 records that she did. This marked her house for safety.

clue_checks.clue: I was the youngest son of Jesse.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:11 confirms Jesse's youngest son kept the sheep, but the verse does not name David. The identification comes from 16:12-13 (and 17:14, 'David was the youngest'), so the cited text alone does not fully tie the clue to David.

clue_checks.clue: I played the harp for King Saul.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:23 explicitly says David took an harp and played for Saul.

clue_checks.clue: I defeated Goliath.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:49-50 says David slew the Philistine with a sling and a stone. Goliath is named in the chapter (17:4, 17:23).

clue_checks.clue: I became king over Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 5:3 says the elders anointed David king over Israel. This clue alone also fits Saul and Solomon, but the full clue set fits only David.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Tishbite.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:1 explicitly calls him 'Elijah the Tishbite.'

clue_checks.clue: Ravens fed me by the brook Cherith.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:3-6 says the ravens brought Elijah bread and flesh by the brook Cherith.

clue_checks.clue: I challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:19-24 shows Elijah gathering the prophets of Baal to mount Carmel and proposing the test of the God that answers by fire.

clue_checks.clue: I went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:11 says 'Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.'

clue_checks.clue: I was of the tribe of Benjamin.
clue_checks.reason: In 1 Samuel 9:21 Saul calls himself 'a Benjamite.' Jonathan was also a Benjamite, but an early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: From my shoulders upward I was higher than any of the people.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 9:2 says this of Saul nearly word for word.

clue_checks.clue: Samuel anointed me as Israel's first king.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 9:17 says he 'shall reign over my people,' and 10:1 shows Samuel anointing him 'captain over his inheritance.' The word 'first' is not in these verses, though it is the clear sense of the narrative.

clue_checks.clue: I consulted a woman at Endor.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 28:7-8 shows Saul going to the woman with a familiar spirit at Endor to enquire of her.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was Bathsheba.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:24 says Bath-sheba bore a son to David and he called his name Solomon. None of the other options had Bathsheba as mother.

clue_checks.clue: I asked God for an understanding heart.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:9 is Solomon's prayer asking for 'an understanding heart'. Verse 5 identifies the speaker as Solomon, and the explanation passage (3:10-12) names him.

clue_checks.clue: I built the temple in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 6:14: 'So Solomon built the house, and finished it.' David planned the temple but did not build it.

clue_checks.clue: I judged between two women who both claimed one baby.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:16-27 records the king judging between two harlots who each claimed the living child. The context makes clear the king is Solomon.

clue_checks.clue: I was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
clue_checks.reason: Neh 1:11 says 'I was the king's cupbearer,' and Neh 2:1 names Artaxerxes and shows Nehemiah serving him wine.

clue_checks.clue: I wept over Jerusalem's broken walls.
clue_checks.reason: Neh 1:3-4: hearing the wall was broken down, he 'sat down and wept, and mourned.'

clue_checks.clue: I led the rebuilding of the city wall.
clue_checks.reason: Neh 2:17-18: Nehemiah calls the people to build the wall, and they respond, 'Let us rise up and build.'

clue_checks.clue: The wall was finished in fifty-two days.
clue_checks.reason: Neh 6:15 states the wall was finished 'in fifty and two days.'

clue_checks.clue: I was raised by my cousin Mordecai.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:7 calls Esther Mordecai's 'uncle's daughter', which makes her his cousin, and says he 'brought up' and 'took [her] for his own daughter.'

clue_checks.clue: I became queen in Persia.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 1:3 places the king's reign in Persia and Media. Esther 2:17 says the king 'made her queen instead of Vashti.' Vashti was also queen in Persia, but an early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I said: If I perish, I perish.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 4:16 quotes Esther saying 'and if I perish, I perish.'

clue_checks.clue: The feast of Purim remembers my people's deliverance.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 9:22 and 9:26-28 describe the Jews' rest from their enemies and establish the days of Purim as a lasting memorial. This fits Esther's people, the Jews.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet, the son of Amittai.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 14:25 names 'his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet.'

clue_checks.clue: I fled from God's call on a ship.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 1:3 says Jonah fled 'from the presence of the LORD' and boarded a ship going to Tarshish.

clue_checks.clue: I spent three days inside a great fish.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 1:17 says Jonah was in the belly of the fish 'three days and three nights.'

clue_checks.clue: I was displeased when Nineveh repented.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 3:10 says Nineveh turned from their evil way, and Jonah 4:1 says 'it displeased Jonah exceedingly.'

clue_checks.clue: I saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year King Uzziah died.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:1 says this nearly word for word. Isaiah narrates in the first person, and the book is his (Isaiah 1:1).

clue_checks.clue: A seraph touched my lips with a live coal.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:6-7 says a seraphim laid a live coal upon his mouth and said it had touched his lips.

clue_checks.clue: I answered: Here am I; send me.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:8 quotes this directly.

clue_checks.clue: I prophesied of a child called Immanuel.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 7:14 foretells a son who shall be called Immanuel. The context (7:3, 7:13) shows Isaiah speaking it to Ahaz.

clue_checks.clue: I was taken captive to Babylon as a young man.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:1-6 describes Nebuchadnezzar besieging Jerusalem and having 'children' of Judah brought to serve in his palace, and names Daniel among them. The passage does not use the word 'captive', but the context clearly supports it.

clue_checks.clue: I purposed not to defile myself with the king's meat.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:8 says nearly word for word that Daniel 'purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat'.

clue_checks.clue: I read the writing on the wall.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 5:25-28 gives the writing and Daniel's interpretation, which implies he read it. The 'wall' detail comes from Daniel 5:5 and is not in the cited verses. This is minor.

clue_checks.clue: I was delivered from the den of lions.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 6:22-23 records God shutting the lions' mouths and Daniel being taken up unhurt.

clue_checks.clue: God said He knew me before He formed me in the belly.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 1:5 states, 'Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee,' spoken to Jeremiah.

clue_checks.clue: I protested that I was only a child.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 1:6 says, 'I cannot speak: for I am a child.' Adding 'only' is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was let down into a dungeon full of mire.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 38:6 says they let Jeremiah down with cords into a dungeon with 'no water, but mire,' and he sank in it.

clue_checks.clue: Baruch wrote my words on a roll.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 36:4 says Baruch wrote from Jeremiah's mouth, upon a roll of a book.

clue_checks.clue: I was chief among the publicans.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:2 states Zacchaeus 'was the chief among the publicans.'

clue_checks.clue: I was rich.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:2 says 'and he was rich.'

clue_checks.clue: I was little of stature.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:3 says 'he was little of stature.'

clue_checks.clue: I climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:4 says he 'climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him.'

clue_checks.clue: My father Zacharias was a priest.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 calls Zacharias a priest, and Luke 1:13 says his son is to be named John.

clue_checks.clue: I wore raiment of camel's hair.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 3:4 says John 'had his raiment of camel's hair.' Elijah is called 'an hairy man' in 2 Kings 1:8, but camel's hair is never stated for him, and a single early clue loosely fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I ate locusts and wild honey.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 3:4 says 'his meat was locusts and wild honey.'

clue_checks.clue: I baptized Jesus in the Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 1:9 says Jesus 'was baptized of John in Jordan.'

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Nazareth of Galilee.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:26-27 says Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, a city of Galilee, to the virgin named Mary, so she was there. Luke 2:4 also places Joseph's home in Nazareth.

clue_checks.clue: The angel Gabriel was sent to me.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:26-27 states that Gabriel was sent from God to a virgin whose name was Mary.

clue_checks.clue: I was espoused to Joseph.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:27 says she was a virgin espoused to a man named Joseph.

clue_checks.clue: I gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:4-7 places Mary in Bethlehem, where she brought forth her firstborn son. Luke 2:21 says his name was called JESUS.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve, called Didymus.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:24 calls Thomas 'one of the twelve, called Didymus.'

clue_checks.clue: I was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:19 describes Jesus appearing to the assembled disciples that evening, and John 20:24 says Thomas 'was not with them when Jesus came.' 'First appeared' is fair within John's account of appearances to the gathered disciples, though Jesus had already appeared to Mary Magdalene (John 20:14-16) and, per Luke 24:34, to Simon.

clue_checks.clue: I wanted to see the print of the nails.
clue_checks.reason: In John 20:25 Thomas says, 'Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails... I will not believe.'

clue_checks.clue: I said: My Lord and my God.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:28 quotes Thomas directly.

clue_checks.clue: I was a fisherman, the brother of Andrew.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:18 names Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother, who were fishers casting a net.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me to become a fisher of men.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:19 records Jesus telling Peter and Andrew, 'I will make you fishers of men.' It also fits Andrew, but that is acceptable for a single clue.

clue_checks.clue: I walked on the water toward Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 14:29 says Peter came down out of the ship and walked on the water to go to Jesus.

clue_checks.clue: I denied Jesus three times before the cock crew.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:75 records Peter remembering Jesus' prediction of a threefold denial before the cock crow and weeping bitterly, which confirms its fulfillment. The denials themselves are narrated in 26:69-74.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: John 3:1 calls Nicodemus 'a man of the Pharisees' and 'a ruler of the Jews.'

clue_checks.clue: I came to Jesus by night.
clue_checks.reason: John 3:2 says 'The same came to Jesus by night,' referring to Nicodemus from verse 1.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus told me I must be born again.
clue_checks.reason: In John 3:7 Jesus says to Nicodemus, 'Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.'

clue_checks.clue: I brought myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:39 says Nicodemus 'brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes' for the burial.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of seven chosen to serve the church.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 6:3-5 lists Stephen first among the seven chosen. Philip was also one of the seven, but a single early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was full of faith and power.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 6:8 says verbatim: 'Stephen, full of faith and power.'

clue_checks.clue: As I spoke I saw the heavens opened.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 7:56 has Stephen saying, 'Behold, I see the heavens opened,' during his speech.

clue_checks.clue: I was stoned while a young man named Saul watched.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 7:58 says the witnesses laid their clothes at Saul's feet, which places him present. It does not explicitly say he 'watched'; Acts 8:1 and 22:20 make that clearer. This is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: My name is interpreted 'the son of consolation'.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 4:36 says Joses was surnamed Barnabas, 'being interpreted, The son of consolation.'

clue_checks.clue: I sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 4:37 says that, having land, he sold it and laid the money at the apostles' feet.

clue_checks.clue: I brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:26-27 says Barnabas took Saul in Jerusalem and brought him to the apostles.

clue_checks.clue: I travelled with Paul on his first missionary journey.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 13:2-4 says Barnabas and Saul were separated and sent forth to Seleucia and Cyprus. 'First missionary journey' is a standard label, and Acts 13:9 identifies Saul as Paul. Mark also fits this clue alone (Acts 13:5), but the earlier clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: I was born in Tarsus.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 22:3 Paul says he was 'born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia.'

clue_checks.clue: I once persecuted the church.
clue_checks.reason: In Galatians 1:13 Paul writes that 'beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.'

clue_checks.clue: A light from heaven blinded me near Damascus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:3-8 describes a light from heaven near Damascus, after which Saul 'saw no man.' Acts 22:11 confirms he 'could not see for the glory of that light.'

clue_checks.clue: I wrote many letters to the churches.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Peter 3:15-16 refers to 'all his epistles,' so Paul wrote several letters. It does not say they were addressed 'to the churches.' This is a minor, acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Bethany.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1 names Lazarus 'of Bethany.'

clue_checks.clue: My sisters were Mary and Martha.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1-2 calls Bethany the town of Mary and her sister Martha and says Mary's 'brother Lazarus was sick.' Martha is Mary's sister, so both are his sisters.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus wept near my grave.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:35 records 'Jesus wept' after he was told 'come and see.' Verse 38 says he then 'cometh to the grave,' so the weeping seems to happen on the way, before he reaches the grave. 'Near my grave' slightly overstates the location, but the gist holds.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me out of the tomb.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:43-44 has Jesus cry 'Lazarus, come forth,' and the dead man came forth.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1-2 calls Bethany 'the town of Mary and her sister Martha' and names Lazarus as Mary's brother. It does not say outright that Martha lived with them or that Lazarus was her brother; that is only implied here. John 11:5 or 11:19-21 would state the sibling tie more clearly.

clue_checks.clue: I was cumbered about much serving.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:40 says this of Martha almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said my sister had chosen the good part.
clue_checks.reason: In Luke 10:42 Jesus says Mary 'hath chosen that good part', and Luke 10:39 identifies Mary as Martha's sister.

clue_checks.clue: I welcomed Jesus into my house.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:38 says 'a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a seller of purple.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:14 explicitly calls Lydia 'a seller of purple.'

clue_checks.clue: I came from the city of Thyatira.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:14 says Lydia was 'of the city of Thyatira.'

clue_checks.clue: I heard Paul speak by a riverside at Philippi.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:12-14 places Paul's company at Philippi, going out 'by a river side' and speaking to the women there. Lydia 'heard us' and attended to Paul's words.

clue_checks.clue: My household was baptized.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:15 says 'when she was baptized, and her household.'

clue_checks.clue: My father was Enoch.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:21 states Enoch begat Methuselah.

clue_checks.clue: My son was Lamech.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:25 states Methuselah begat Lamech.

clue_checks.clue: I was Noah's grandfather.
clue_checks.reason: Methuselah begat Lamech (5:25), and Lamech begat Noah (5:28-29), so Methuselah is Noah's grandfather.

clue_checks.clue: I lived nine hundred sixty and nine years.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:27 gives exactly 969 years for Methuselah.

clue_checks.clue: My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice shared unfeigned faith.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 1:5 says the unfeigned faith dwelt first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. It is addressed to Timothy.

clue_checks.clue: I was Paul's young companion.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:1-3 shows Paul taking Timotheus with him, and 1 Timothy 4:12 refers to his youth. The clue is early and generic, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: Paul called me his dearly beloved son.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 1:2 says 'To Timothy, my dearly beloved son.'

clue_checks.clue: Two New Testament letters are addressed to me.
clue_checks.reason: The salutations of 1 Timothy 1:2 and 2 Timothy 1:2 are both addressed to Timothy. Titus received only one letter, so this clue distinguishes him from the other options.

clue_checks.clue: I was a tiller of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 states that Cain was a tiller of the ground, while Abel was a keeper of sheep.

clue_checks.clue: God did not respect my offering.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:5 says that unto Cain and his offering the LORD had not respect.

clue_checks.clue: I asked: Am I my brother's keeper?
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:9 records Cain answering the LORD, 'I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?'

clue_checks.clue: God set a mark upon me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:15 says the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

clue_checks.clue: I was formed of the dust of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:7 says the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground. This man is the one named Adam in 2:19-20, so the clue fits Adam.

clue_checks.clue: I gave names to the animals.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:20 explicitly says Adam gave names to all cattle, fowl, and beasts of the field.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the garden of Eden.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:15 says the LORD God put the man into the garden of Eden to dress and keep it. This is Adam.

clue_checks.clue: My wife was Eve.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:20 says Adam called his wife's name Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I walked with God.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:22 states Enoch walked with God. Noah also walked with God (Genesis 6:9), but this is an early clue and later clues distinguish Enoch.

clue_checks.clue: I was the father of Methuselah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:21 says Enoch begat Methuselah. This applies uniquely to Enoch among the options.

clue_checks.clue: I was not, for God took me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:24 quotes this nearly verbatim of Enoch.

clue_checks.clue: Hebrews says I was translated so I should not see death.
clue_checks.reason: Hebrews 11:5 states Enoch was translated that he should not see death. Elijah was also taken without dying, but Hebrews names Enoch and the Methuselah clue excludes Elijah.

clue_checks.clue: My husband was Elkanah.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:1-2 names Elkanah as Hannah's husband. Peninnah was also his wife, but this is only the first clue and later clues exclude her.

clue_checks.clue: I prayed silently at Shiloh, and Eli thought I was drunk.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:9-13 places Hannah in Shiloh and says she spoke in her heart, her voice was not heard, and Eli thought she had been drunken.

clue_checks.clue: I vowed to give my son to the LORD.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:11 records her vow to give a man child to the LORD all the days of his life. Saying 'my son' is a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I named my son Samuel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:20 says Hannah bore a son and called his name Samuel.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the land of Uz.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:1 states there was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. The friends are identified by other origins (Temanite, Shuhite, Buzite).

clue_checks.clue: I was perfect and upright.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:1 calls Job 'perfect and upright'.

clue_checks.clue: I lost my children and possessions in a single day.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:13-19 opens with 'there was a day' and has the messengers arriving 'while he was yet speaking'. They report the loss of the oxen, asses, sheep and camels and the deaths of his sons and daughters.

clue_checks.clue: I said: The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away.
clue_checks.reason: These are Job's words, quoted directly in Job 1:21.

clue_checks.clue: I was captain of the host of the king of Syria.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:1 calls Naaman 'captain of the host of the king of Syria.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a leper.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:1 ends 'but he was a leper.' Gehazi was later struck with leprosy, but a single early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: A captive little maid from Israel told of a prophet.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:2-3 says a captive little maid who waited on Naaman's wife spoke of the prophet in Samaria who could recover him.

clue_checks.clue: I dipped myself seven times in the Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:14 says he 'dipped himself seven times in Jordan.'

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve spies.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 13:6 lists Caleb son of Jephunneh as Judah's representative among the spies. The surrounding list (13:4-15) names twelve men, one per tribe. Joshua was also a spy, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I brought back a good report with Joshua.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 14:6-9 records Joshua and Caleb together calling the land 'exceeding good' and urging the people not to fear.

clue_checks.clue: I was eighty-five years old when I asked for my inheritance.
clue_checks.reason: In Joshua 14:10 Caleb says, 'I am this day fourscore and five years old,' while requesting his inheritance.

clue_checks.clue: I asked for the mountain and received Hebron.
clue_checks.reason: In Joshua 14:12-13 Caleb says 'give me this mountain,' and Joshua gives Caleb Hebron for an inheritance.

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Salem.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 14:18 explicitly calls Melchizedek 'king of Salem.'

clue_checks.clue: I was priest of the most high God.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 14:18 says 'he was the priest of the most high God.'

clue_checks.clue: I brought forth bread and wine to Abram.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 14:18 says Melchizedek 'brought forth bread and wine.' The shown text does not name Abram, but in context 'him' in v.17 is Abram returning from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer, and v.19 has Melchizedek blessing Abram.

clue_checks.clue: Abram gave me tithes of all.
clue_checks.reason: Hebrews 7:2 says 'To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all,' and 'whom' refers to Melchizedek in v.1. Abraham and Abram are the same person. Genesis 14:20 also records the tithe.

clue_checks.clue: I was a publican.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 10:3 explicitly calls him 'Matthew the publican.' Zacchaeus was also a publican, but a single early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I sat at the receipt of custom.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 9:9 says Jesus saw Matthew 'sitting at the receipt of custom.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said to me: Follow me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 9:9 records Jesus saying to Matthew, 'Follow me.'

clue_checks.clue: After calling me, Jesus sat at meat in the house with many publicans and sinners.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 9:10 directly follows the call and says Jesus sat at meat in the house with many publicans and sinners. The clue says 'the house' without claiming it was Matthew's, so it matches the text.

clue_checks.clue: Seven devils had gone out of me.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 8:2 names 'Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils.'

clue_checks.clue: I stood by the cross.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:25 lists Mary Magdalene among those who 'stood by the cross of Jesus.'

clue_checks.clue: I came to the tomb while it was yet dark.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:1 says Mary Magdalene came 'early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre.' 'Tomb' is a fair paraphrase of 'sepulchre.'

clue_checks.clue: At first I supposed the risen Jesus was the gardener.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:15 says 'She, supposing him to be the gardener.' Verse 15 itself says only 'she', but the context (John 20:11, 16) identifies her as Mary, and the reference label includes verse 16 ('Jesus saith unto her, Mary').

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:14 calls Judas Iscariot 'one of the twelve.' This also fits Peter, Thomas and Andrew, but it is an early clue and later clues narrow the answer.

clue_checks.clue: I had the bag.
clue_checks.reason: John 12:4-6 names Judas Iscariot and says he 'had the bag, and bare what was put therein.'

clue_checks.clue: I agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:15 shows Judas offering to deliver Jesus, and the chief priests 'covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.'

clue_checks.clue: I betrayed Jesus with a kiss.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:48-49 describes 'he that betrayed him' giving a sign by a kiss and then kissing Jesus. The context (v. 47) identifies him as Judas.

clue_checks.clue: I was a mighty man of wealth in Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:1 calls Boaz 'a mighty man of wealth,' and Ruth 2:4 says he 'came from Beth-lehem.'

clue_checks.clue: I let a Moabite woman glean in my fields.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:6 identifies Ruth as 'the Moabitish damsel,' and in Ruth 2:8 Boaz tells her to glean in his field and not go to another.

clue_checks.clue: I redeemed the inheritance of Elimelech.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:9-10 has Boaz declare 'I have bought all that was Elimelech's.' This fits the kinsman-redemption context, so the clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I married Ruth.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13 says 'So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the first woman.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:22 describes the LORD God making the first woman from the man's rib. Genesis 3:20 identifies this woman as Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I was made from a rib taken from the man.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:22 states the rib taken from man was made into a woman.

clue_checks.clue: The serpent spoke to me in the garden.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:1 says the serpent 'said unto the woman' about the trees of the garden. This woman is Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I am called the mother of all living.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:20 says Adam named her Eve 'because she was the mother of all living.'

clue_checks.clue: I watched over my baby brother at the river.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:4 says 'his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him' by the river's brink. Numbers 26:59 names Miriam as the sister of Moses and Aaron, which identifies her.

clue_checks.clue: I am called a prophetess.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 15:20 calls her 'Miriam the prophetess.' Deborah is also called a prophetess (Judges 4:4), but this is only one early clue and the full set excludes her.

clue_checks.clue: I led the women with a timbrel after the Red Sea crossing.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 15:20 says she took a timbrel and 'all the women went out after her.' The Red Sea setting comes from the surrounding context (Exodus 15:19, the Song of the Sea). That is minor contextual paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was briefly struck with leprosy.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 12:10 says Miriam 'became leprous.' Numbers 12:14-15 limits her exclusion to seven days and says she was then received in again, so 'briefly' is fair.

clue_checks.clue: I drew water for a stranger's camels at a well.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:19-20 shows Rebekah offering and drawing water for all the camels of Abraham's servant, a stranger to her. Rachel came to a well with her father's sheep, but Jacob watered them, not she.

clue_checks.clue: I was the sister of Laban.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:29 states plainly that Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Rachel and Leah were Laban's daughters, not his sisters.

clue_checks.clue: I married Isaac.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 24:67 says Isaac took Rebekah and she became his wife. Of the other options, Sarah was Isaac's mother.

clue_checks.clue: I helped my son Jacob receive his father's blessing.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 27:6-17 shows Rebekah directing Jacob, preparing the savoury meat, and disguising him in Esau's raiment and goat skins so he could obtain Isaac's blessing.

clue_checks.clue: I was a son of Zebedee.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 names 'John his brother' alongside James the son of Zebedee, with Zebedee their father. It also fits James, but early clues may overlap.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus surnamed my brother and me Boanerges.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 3:17 says Jesus surnamed James and John 'Boanerges.' It fits James equally, which is acceptable for a mid-sequence clue.

clue_checks.clue: Tradition identifies me as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
clue_checks.reason: John 21:20 mentions the disciple whom Jesus loved but does not name him. The clue openly frames the identification as tradition, so it is not misleading, though the text alone does not establish it.

clue_checks.clue: I was on the isle of Patmos for the word of God.
clue_checks.reason: Revelation 1:9 says 'I John... was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God.' That this John is the apostle is traditional rather than stated, a point the explanation acknowledges.

clue_checks.clue: My mother laughed when my birth was promised.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 18:12 records Sarah laughing. The verse does not name Isaac or state the promise itself, which appears in 18:10. The context supports the clue, but the cited verse alone does not show the link to Isaac.

clue_checks.clue: My father was a hundred years old when I was born.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 21:5 says Abraham was an hundred years old when his son Isaac was born.

clue_checks.clue: I was laid on an altar in the land of Moriah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 22:2 names the land of Moriah, and 22:9 says Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the altar.

clue_checks.clue: My sons were Esau and Jacob.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:25-26 names Esau and Jacob as the twins and says Isaac was threescore years old when they were born.

clue_checks.clue: I was Abram's nephew.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 12:5 calls Lot Abram's 'brother's son,' which means nephew. Terah was Abram's father and Nahor his brother. Laban was Nahor's grandson, not Abram's nephew.

clue_checks.clue: I chose all the plain of Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 13:11 says almost word for word: 'Lot chose him all the plain of Jordan.'

clue_checks.clue: Two angels came to my house in Sodom.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 19:1-3 says two angels came to Sodom, Lot urged them to his house, and they 'entered into his house.'

clue_checks.clue: My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 19:26 says 'his wife looked back from behind him,' and the surrounding verses make clear this is Lot's wife.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Laban.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:16 names Rachel as Laban's younger daughter. The clue also fits Leah, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: Jacob served seven years for me, and they seemed but a few days.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 29:20 matches this clue nearly word for word, and it applies only to Rachel.

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:24 lists Joseph and Benjamin as the sons of Rachel.

clue_checks.clue: I died on the way to Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 35:19 says Rachel died and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth-lehem.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Levite and the brother of Moses.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 4:14 reads 'Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother?', spoken to Moses.

clue_checks.clue: I spoke to Pharaoh on Moses' behalf.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 7:2 says 'Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh', relaying what Moses was commanded.

clue_checks.clue: I made a golden calf when the people asked.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 32:1-4 says the people asked Aaron to make gods, and he fashioned a molten calf from their golden earrings, so 'golden calf' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: My rod budded and yielded almonds.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 17:8 says the rod of Aaron 'was budded... and yielded almonds.'

clue_checks.clue: I am called a soothsayer.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 13:22 calls him "Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer."

clue_checks.clue: Balak, king of Moab, sent for me to curse Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 22:4-6 says Balak, king of the Moabites, sent messengers to Balaam asking him to "curse me this people," meaning Israel come out of Egypt.

clue_checks.clue: An angel with a drawn sword stood in my way.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 22:31 says Balaam saw the angel of the LORD "standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand."

clue_checks.clue: My ass spoke to me.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 22:28 says the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she spoke to Balaam.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest of Midian.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:1 calls Jethro 'the priest of Midian.'

clue_checks.clue: I was Moses' father-in-law.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 18:1 names Jethro as 'Moses' father in law.'

clue_checks.clue: Moses kept my flock near Horeb.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:1 says Moses kept Jethro's flock and led it to Horeb, the mountain of God.

clue_checks.clue: I advised Moses to appoint rulers to judge the people.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 18:17-22 records Moses' father-in-law counseling him to set rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens to judge the people. These verses do not name him, but Exodus 18:1 in the same chapter identifies him as Jethro.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest at Shiloh.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:9 places Hannah at Shiloh and calls Eli 'the priest' sitting by a post of the temple of the LORD there.

clue_checks.clue: I thought Hannah was drunken as she prayed.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:13-14 says Eli thought she had been drunken and rebuked her.

clue_checks.clue: My sons Hophni and Phinehas were wicked.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:3 names Hophni and Phinehas as Eli's sons, and 2:12 calls them 'sons of Belial' who knew not the LORD. 'Wicked' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I fell backward and died when I heard the ark was taken.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 4:17-18 says that when the ark was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his seat, broke his neck, and died.

clue_checks.clue: I was the son of King Saul.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 14:1 names 'Jonathan the son of Saul.' Ishbosheth was also Saul's son, but this is an early clue and later clues narrow the answer.

clue_checks.clue: I climbed up to a Philistine garrison with my armourbearer.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 14:13 says Jonathan climbed up on hands and feet with his armourbearer after him. The garrison is named in the surrounding context (14:1, 14:11-12).

clue_checks.clue: My soul was knit with the soul of David.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 18:1 matches nearly word for word.

clue_checks.clue: I warned David by shooting arrows.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 20:20-22 sets out the arrow signal, and 20:36-37 shows Jonathan shooting and calling 'Is not the arrow beyond thee?', the warning sign.

clue_checks.clue: I was a champion of the Philistines.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 says 'there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath.'

clue_checks.clue: I came from Gath.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 calls him 'Goliath, of Gath.' Achish was also of Gath, but a single early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: My height was six cubits and a span.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:4 gives his height as 'six cubits and a span.'

clue_checks.clue: A shepherd boy struck me down with a sling and a stone.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:15 shows David feeding his father's sheep. 1 Samuel 17:49-50 records David slaying the Philistine 'with a sling and with a stone.' Calling David a 'boy' is a minor paraphrase; the KJV elsewhere calls him 'but a youth' (17:33, 42).

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet in David's court.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 7:2 calls Nathan 'the prophet' and shows him speaking with King David. Gad would also fit, but this is an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I told David his son would build God's house.
clue_checks.reason: The word came to Nathan to tell David (7:4-5) that David's seed 'out of thy bowels' would build a house for God's name (7:12-13).

clue_checks.clue: I told David a parable about a poor man's ewe lamb.
clue_checks.reason: In 2 Samuel 12:1-4 Nathan tells the parable of the rich man and the poor man's one ewe lamb.

clue_checks.clue: I said to David, Thou art the man.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:7 quotes Nathan's words exactly.

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:3 explicitly identifies Bath-sheba as 'the wife of Uriah the Hittite.'

clue_checks.clue: King David saw me washing as he walked on his roof.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 11:2 says David walked upon the roof of the king's house and from the roof saw a woman washing herself. This is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I became the mother of Solomon.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:24 states Bath-sheba bare a son and he called his name Solomon.

clue_checks.clue: My son King Solomon set a seat for me at his right hand.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 2:19 says Solomon caused a seat to be set for the king's mother, and she sat on his right hand.

clue_checks.clue: I was a son of King David.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 3:3 names Absalom as the third son. The context (3:2, 'unto David were sons born in Hebron') makes clear these are David's sons. Amnon, Adonijah and Solomon were also David's sons, but this is an early clue, so that is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 15:6 says it directly: 'so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.' This is unique to Absalom among the options.

clue_checks.clue: I led a rebellion against my father.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 15:10-12 describes Absalom proclaiming himself king in Hebron and a strong, growing conspiracy against David's rule. Adonijah's later attempt (1 Kings 1) fits this clue on its own, but the full set of clues points only to Absalom.

clue_checks.clue: My head caught in an oak as my mule went on.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 18:9 says 'his head caught hold of the oak... and the mule that was under him went away.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:29 says Ahab began to reign over Israel. The clue also fits Jeroboam, Omri and Jehu, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I married Jezebel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:31 says he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal. Context (v.30) identifies the subject as Ahab.

clue_checks.clue: I asked Elijah, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:17 quotes Ahab verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: I wanted Naboth's vineyard for a garden of herbs.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 21:2 has Ahab asking for the vineyard 'for a garden of herbs.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a king of Judah.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:1 names Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah. All four options were kings of Judah, which is acceptable for an opening clue.

clue_checks.clue: I broke in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 18:4 says he 'brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made.' This is unique to Hezekiah.

clue_checks.clue: Isaiah told me to set my house in order.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 38:1 has Isaiah telling the sick Hezekiah, 'Set thine house in order.'

clue_checks.clue: God added fifteen years to my life.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 38:5 says 'I will add unto thy days fifteen years.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest and a ready scribe in the law of Moses.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 7:6 calls Ezra 'a ready scribe in the law of Moses,' and Ezra 7:11 calls him 'Ezra the priest, the scribe.'

clue_checks.clue: I went up from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes.
clue_checks.reason: Ezra 7:1 places the events 'in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia,' and 7:6 says 'This Ezra went up from Babylon.' Nehemiah also served under Artaxerxes, but the full set of clues excludes him.

clue_checks.clue: I read the book of the law to the people.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 8:2-3 says Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation and read from it from morning until midday.

clue_checks.clue: I stood upon a pulpit of wood.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 8:4 says 'Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the daughter of the king of the Zidonians.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:31 calls Jezebel 'the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians.'

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of King Ahab.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 16:31 says 'he took to wife Jezebel.' The 'he' is Ahab, named in the surrounding verses (16:29-30). The quoted verse itself does not name Ahab, but the context makes this clear.

clue_checks.clue: I threatened Elijah's life after Mount Carmel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:1-2 follows Elijah's slaying of the prophets at Carmel. Jezebel sends a messenger vowing to make his life 'as the life of one of them by to morrow.'

clue_checks.clue: I arranged Naboth's death to take his vineyard.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 21:7-15 shows Jezebel writing letters in Ahab's name to have Naboth falsely accused and stoned. She then tells Ahab to take possession of the vineyard.

clue_checks.clue: I became king of Judah at eight years old.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:1 states Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem. Joash was seven (2 Kings 11:21), so this clue does not fit him.

clue_checks.clue: The book of the law was found in the temple in my reign.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:8 records Hilkiah finding the book of the law in the house of the LORD, but the verse itself does not name the king. The link to Josiah's reign comes from 22:3 (the eighteenth year of king Josiah). The context supports the clue, but the quoted verse alone does not.

clue_checks.clue: I rent my clothes when it was read to me.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 22:11 says the king rent his clothes when he heard the words of the book of the law. Verse 10 confirms Shaphan read it before the king.

clue_checks.clue: I kept a great passover.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 23:21-23 describes Josiah's unparalleled passover in his eighteenth year. Hezekiah also kept a great passover (2 Chronicles 30), but the earlier clues (age eight, book found, rent clothes) rule him out, so the full set fits only Josiah.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest of the course of Abia.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 names Zacharias as a priest of the course of Abia.

clue_checks.clue: An angel appeared to me by the altar of incense.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:11 says an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense.

clue_checks.clue: I was struck dumb because I did not believe.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:20 says he would be dumb and unable to speak because he did not believe the angel's words.

clue_checks.clue: I wrote: His name is John.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:63 says he asked for a writing table and wrote, 'His name is John.'

clue_checks.clue: I was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 1:1 says Amos 'was among the herdmen of Tekoa.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a gatherer of sycomore fruit.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 7:14 says 'I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit.'

clue_checks.clue: I said I was no prophet, neither a prophet's son.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 7:14 records Amos telling Amaziah, 'I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son.'

clue_checks.clue: I cried: let judgment run down as waters.
clue_checks.reason: Amos 5:24 contains these words in Amos's book, but in context (5:21-24) they are the LORD's words that Amos delivers. Saying 'I cried' slightly overstates Amos's personal voice, though it is acceptable as prophetic proclamation.

clue_checks.clue: I was of the daughters of Aaron.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 states that Zacharias's wife Elisabeth was of the daughters of Aaron.

clue_checks.clue: I was barren and well stricken in years.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:7 says Elisabeth was barren and that they both were well stricken in years.

clue_checks.clue: My babe leaped in my womb when Mary greeted me.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:41 says the babe leaped in her womb when Elisabeth heard Mary's salutation.

clue_checks.clue: I was the mother of John the Baptist.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:57-60 shows Elisabeth bore a son and insisted he be called John. The title 'the Baptist' is not in this passage, though the identification is well established elsewhere in Luke.

clue_checks.clue: I was a priest among the captives by the river Chebar.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 1:1-3 has the speaker 'among the captives by the river of Chebar' and names 'Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi' by the river Chebar.

clue_checks.clue: I saw wheels whose rings were full of eyes.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 1:18 says 'their rings were full of eyes round about them four.' In context (1:15-16) the rings belong to the wheels, so this is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I lay on my side for many days as a sign.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 4:4-6 records God's command to lie on the left side 390 days and the right side 40 days as a sign. The passage gives the command, not an explicit account of Ezekiel carrying it out. The clue is still a reasonable inference.

clue_checks.clue: I prophesied to a valley of dry bones.
clue_checks.reason: Ezekiel 37:4 commands prophesying to the dry bones. The 'valley' detail comes from 37:1-2, which is not quoted. The clue is accurate to Ezekiel 37 overall.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet to Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:1 says the word of the LORD came to Hosea and dates it by the kings of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel. It does not explicitly say he prophesied to Israel, though the book's content does. As an early clue it also fits Amos, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I obeyed God and took Gomer as my wife.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:3 shows Hosea taking Gomer the daughter of Diblaim ('So he went'). The command he obeyed is in 1:2, which is not quoted, and 1:3 does not use the word 'wife', so the obedience is only implied.

clue_checks.clue: I named a son Loammi.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 1:8-9 records God commanding 'Call his name Lo-ammi'. The command is directed at Hosea, but the text does not narrate Hosea actually doing the naming. The spelling difference is minor.

clue_checks.clue: I bought a woman for fifteen pieces of silver and barley.
clue_checks.reason: Hosea 3:2 says 'I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a just and devout man in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:25 names Simeon as a man in Jerusalem who was 'just and devout.'

clue_checks.clue: The Holy Ghost revealed I would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:26 says it was revealed to him by the Holy Ghost that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ.

clue_checks.clue: I took the child Jesus up in my arms in the temple.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:27-28 says he came into the temple and took the child Jesus up in his arms.

clue_checks.clue: I said: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:29 quotes these words exactly.

clue_checks.clue: I was from Cana of Galilee.
clue_checks.reason: John 21:2 names 'Nathanael of Cana in Galilee.'

clue_checks.clue: I asked: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
clue_checks.reason: John 1:46 records Nathanael saying exactly this.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus saw me under the fig tree.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:48: 'when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:47 matches the clue verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:44 states Philip was of Bethsaida. Andrew was also from there, but this is an early clue and later clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said to me, Follow me.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:43 says Jesus found Philip and said unto him, Follow me.

clue_checks.clue: I told Nathanael: Come and see.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:46 records Philip saying to Nathanael, Come and see.

clue_checks.clue: I asked Jesus: Lord, shew us the Father.
clue_checks.reason: John 14:8 quotes Philip saying, Lord, shew us the Father.

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophetess of the tribe of Aser.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:36 calls Anna 'a prophetess... of the tribe of Aser.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a widow of about fourscore and four years.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:37 uses this exact wording.

clue_checks.clue: I served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:37 says she 'served God with fastings and prayers night and day.'

clue_checks.clue: I gave thanks when the child Jesus was brought to the temple.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:27 sets the scene of the parents bringing the child Jesus into the temple. Luke 2:38 says Anna, 'coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord.'

clue_checks.clue: I was from Bethsaida.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:44 calls Bethsaida 'the city of Andrew and Peter.' It also fits Philip, but this is the first clue, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of two who heard John the Baptist speak and followed Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:40 explicitly names Andrew as one of the two who heard John speak and followed Jesus.

clue_checks.clue: I brought my brother Simon to Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: John 1:41-42 says he found his brother Simon and brought him to Jesus.

clue_checks.clue: I told Jesus of a lad with five barley loaves.
clue_checks.reason: John 6:8-9 names Andrew as the one who told Jesus about the lad with five barley loaves and two small fishes.

clue_checks.clue: I was of the house and lineage of David.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:4 says Joseph 'was of the house and lineage of David.'

clue_checks.clue: An angel told me in a dream not to fear to take Mary as my wife.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 1:20 says the angel appeared to Joseph in a dream and told him to 'fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife.'

clue_checks.clue: I took the young child and his mother into Egypt by night.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:14 says he 'took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.'

clue_checks.clue: People called Jesus the carpenter's son.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 13:55 records people asking 'Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary?' Applying 'the carpenter' to Joseph, Mary's husband, is a clear and standard reading of the context.

clue_checks.clue: I was the Roman governor of Judaea.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 3:1 says 'Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa.' Felix was also a governor, but this is an early clue, and the later clues narrow the answer to Pilate.

clue_checks.clue: My wife sent word about a dream concerning a just man.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:19 says his wife sent word about 'that just man' and a dream. The surrounding context (27:17) identifies 'he' as Pilate.

clue_checks.clue: I asked: What is truth?
clue_checks.reason: John 18:38 reads 'Pilate saith unto him, What is truth?'

clue_checks.clue: I washed my hands before the multitude.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 27:24 says Pilate 'washed his hands before the multitude.'

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Joppa.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:36 says there was at Joppa a disciple named Tabitha (Dorcas).

clue_checks.clue: I was full of good works and almsdeeds.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:36 says she was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.

clue_checks.clue: I made coats and garments that the widows showed.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:39 says the widows were showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made.

clue_checks.clue: Peter said to me, arise, and I opened my eyes.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:40 says Peter said, 'Tabitha, arise,' and she opened her eyes.

clue_checks.clue: I was high priest that same year.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:49 names Caiaphas as 'the high priest that same year.'

clue_checks.clue: I said it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:50 continues Caiaphas's speech begun in 11:49 and says 'it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people.' John 18:14 also confirms Caiaphas gave this counsel.

clue_checks.clue: Annas was my father-in-law.
clue_checks.reason: John 18:13 says Annas 'was father in law to Caiaphas.'

clue_checks.clue: Annas sent Jesus to me bound.
clue_checks.reason: John 18:24 says 'Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 5:34 calls Gamaliel 'a Pharisee' and 'a doctor of the law.'

clue_checks.clue: I was had in reputation among all the people.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 5:34 quotes this phrase directly about Gamaliel.

clue_checks.clue: I told the council to let the apostles alone.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 5:38 has Gamaliel say 'Refrain from these men, and let them alone.' The surrounding context (5:34-35) shows he was addressing the council about the apostles.

clue_checks.clue: Paul was brought up at my feet.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 22:3 Paul says he was 'brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a centurion of the Italian band.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:1 names Cornelius as a centurion of the Italian band. Julius belonged to 'Augustus' band' (Acts 27:1), so he is not a match.

clue_checks.clue: I was a devout man who prayed to God alway.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:2 says this nearly verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: An angel told me to send to Joppa for Peter.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:3-5 records an angel telling Cornelius to send men to Joppa for Simon Peter.

clue_checks.clue: The Holy Ghost fell on all who heard Peter speak in my house.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 10:44 confirms the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard. Acts 10:24 shows Cornelius gathered his kinsmen and friends, but neither cited verse says it happened in his house. That is stated in Acts 10:25-27 and 11:12. This is a minor added detail, still accurate to the narrative.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Jew born at Alexandria.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:24 states 'a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria.'

clue_checks.clue: I was an eloquent man, mighty in the scriptures.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:24 calls Apollos 'an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures.'

clue_checks.clue: Aquila and Priscilla taught me the way of God more perfectly.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:26 says Aquila and Priscilla 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.' 'Taught' is a fair paraphrase. The clue also rules out the Aquila option.

clue_checks.clue: Paul wrote that he planted and I watered.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Corinthians 3:6 reads 'I have planted, Apollos watered.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a chief man among the brethren.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:22 names Judas Barsabas and Silas as 'chief men among the brethren.'

clue_checks.clue: I travelled with Paul after he parted from Barnabas.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 15:39-40 says that after the sharp contention Barnabas took Mark, and 'Paul chose Silas, and departed.'

clue_checks.clue: I was beaten and put in the stocks with Paul at Philippi.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:12 places them at Philippi. Acts 16:19 names Paul and Silas as the men seized. Acts 16:22-24 records the beating with many stripes and their feet made fast in the stocks.

clue_checks.clue: At midnight Paul and I prayed and sang praises.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:25 states this directly of Paul and Silas.

clue_checks.clue: My husband Aquila and I were tentmakers.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:3 says 'by their occupation they were tentmakers,' which refers to Aquila and Priscilla, named as husband and wife in 18:2.

clue_checks.clue: We came from Italy when Claudius commanded the Jews to leave Rome.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:2 says Aquila was 'lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla' because 'Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome.'

clue_checks.clue: Paul stayed and worked with us in Corinth.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:1-3 places Paul in Corinth, where 'he abode with them, and wrought.'

clue_checks.clue: We expounded the way of God more perfectly to Apollos.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 18:26 says Aquila and Priscilla 'expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly,' and 'him' is Apollos (18:24).

clue_checks.clue: I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:17 explicitly calls her 'Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite.'

clue_checks.clue: Sisera fled to my tent.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:17 says Sisera 'fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael.'

clue_checks.clue: I gave him milk when he asked for water.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:19: he asked for 'a little water,' and she 'opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink.'

clue_checks.clue: I drove a nail of the tent into his temples.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:21: Jael 'took a nail of the tent... and smote the nail into his temples.'

clue_checks.clue: My husband Nabal was churlish.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 25:3 names Nabal as the husband of Abigail and says he was 'churlish and evil in his doings.'

clue_checks.clue: I brought bread, wine and figs to David's men.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 25:18 lists loaves, wine and cakes of figs that Abigail gathered. The verse itself does not say they were for David's men; that comes from the surrounding context (v.27). This is a minor gap.

clue_checks.clue: I persuaded David not to shed blood.
clue_checks.reason: In 1 Samuel 25:33 David blesses her advice, which 'kept me this day from coming to shed blood.' In context he is addressing Abigail.

clue_checks.clue: After Nabal died, I became David's wife.
clue_checks.reason: Verses 38-39 record Nabal's death and David's proposal. Verse 42 says Abigail 'became his wife.'

clue_checks.clue: I was king in Judaea when Jesus was born.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:1 says Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea 'in the days of Herod the king.'

clue_checks.clue: I was troubled when wise men asked for the King of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:2-3 records the wise men's question and says 'Herod the king... was troubled.'

clue_checks.clue: I told the wise men to bring me word again.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:8 says 'bring me word again'; the 'he' refers to Herod, named in the surrounding verses (2:7).

clue_checks.clue: I ordered the children in Bethlehem slain.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 2:16 says Herod 'sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem.' Sending forth to slay is fairly paraphrased as ordering the killing.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the valley of Sorek.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:4 describes Delilah as 'a woman in the valley of Sorek,' which reasonably supports that she lived there.

clue_checks.clue: The lords of the Philistines offered me silver.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:5 says the Philistine lords each promised her eleven hundred pieces of silver.

clue_checks.clue: I asked a strong man the secret of his strength.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:6 records Delilah asking Samson wherein his great strength lay.

clue_checks.clue: I had his seven locks shaved while he slept.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 16:19 says she made him sleep on her knees and called a man to shave off the seven locks of his head.
